slides: Can recursive self-improvement, R S I, improve a language model's understanding of physics?

AI can now generate scenes that look remarkably real. But the motion often breaks the physics: Newton's laws, energy conservation, whether a ball bounces back off a wall, and whether momentum carries over when objects collide.

So we put an agent in the loop. Claude builds the training environment, generates the data, and writes a verifiable reward: a program that checks the physics. That reward is the signal for reinforcement learning on a small Qwen model.
Here is a correct bounce off a wall, and a failure we catch: the ball passes straight through. Every failure becomes a reward signal.
Here is the success rate on cases the model has never seen, over the course of training.
That is recursive self-improvement, applied to physics. Thank you.
